name: Falcon USD
oneLiner: USDf is Falcon Finance's overcollateralized synthetic dollar minted 1:1 from stablecoins or via dynamic ratios against BTC, ETH, SOL, and altcoin collateral.
collateral: Crypto assets backing USDf and the USDf Earn strategy, including BTC and stablecoins, with delta-neutral hedging on centralized exchanges; tokenized real-world assets (USTB, JAAA, JTRSY, plus tokenized gold/equities/CETES) accepted with dynamic overcollateralization ratios
pegMechanism: Overcollateralized synthetic dollar; liquidation mechanisms and arbitrage maintain the $1 peg; delta-neutral strategies power sUSDf yield

applicabilityBasis.summary: USDf is an overcollateralized synthetic dollar backed by crypto assets (BTC, ETH, SOL, stablecoins, altcoins) with delta-neutral strategies — not a fiat-redeemable payment instrument. Issued by Falcon Digital Limited (BVI). Terms of Use explicitly prohibit US persons: 'The Falcon Assets are not offered or sold, and will not be offered or sold, in the United States or to U.S. Persons.' Falcon Finance created a separate GENIUS-ready product (fUSD, issued by Anchorage Digital Bank N.A.) expressly because USDf cannot serve compliance-constrained US institutions.

genius.notes: USDf is a crypto-collateralized synthetic dollar (mechanismArchetype: synthetic-delta-neutral), not a fiat-backed payment stablecoin. US persons are explicitly excluded from the Terms of Use; the United States is listed as a restricted jurisdiction. Falcon Finance launched a separate GENIUS-ready token (fUSD) issued by Anchorage Digital Bank N.A. (federally chartered) on 2026-05-27 as the compliant US payment stablecoin counterpart — confirming that USDf itself is out of GENIUS scope. A quarterly audit report was published in October 2025 confirming full reserve backing; attestation cadence is quarterly, not monthly.

mintAuthority.summary: USDf uses AccessControl; DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE is a 4/6 Safe and MINTER_ROLE is held by a Falcon-owned PreCollateralizedMinter contract (also admin'd by the Safe). Both confirmed on-chain.

controls.label: USDf default admin Safe
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25294739, hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE=0x00, 0x1e482b60) returned true (confirmed). getOwners() returned 6 owners, getThreshold()=4, guard storage slot=zero, getModules() returned empty array, masterCopy slot=0x41675c (Gnosis Safe 1.4.1). All reads via publicnode RPC.

controls.label: USDf PreCollateralizedMinter
controls.evidence: At block 25294739, hasRole(MINTER_ROLE=0x9f2df0fe, 0x3A4F41) returned true (confirmed via Blockscout RoleGranted scan). Contract is named PreCollateralizedMinter (verified source, 3395 bytes). hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, 0x1e482b60) on this contract returned true — the admin Safe controls it. No RoleRevoked events found.

review.evidence: At block 25294739: DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE = 4/6 Safe 0x1e482b60 (RPC-confirmed: 6 owners, no modules, guard=zero, masterCopy Gnosis Safe 1.4.1). MINTER_ROLE = PreCollateralizedMinter 0x3A4F41 (verified source), which is itself admin'd by the same Safe. Blockscout event scan confirms no revocations. All mint-capable on-chain surfaces confirmed.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Falcon Finance states USDf uses Chainlink CCIP and the Cross-Chain Token standard for native cross-chain transfers. Because supported-chain supply movement depends on CCIP validation, the route is scored as external-validated-network.
